models_evaluated: bpMRI-based deep learning model for prostate cancer lesion detection

links.outcome: AI sensitivity for recurrent prostate cancer versus radiologist on post-radiotherapy patients
links.effect: AI model developed on treatment-naive patients had lower sensitivity than prospective radiology: patient-level 76.1% vs 91.3% (p=0.02); lesion-level 71.4% vs 87.5% (p=0.01).
links.quote: The AI model performance was lower than the prospective radiology interpretation (Rad) on a patient-(AI: 76.1% vs. Rad: 91.3%, p = 0.02) and lesion-level (AI: 71.4% vs. Rad: 87.5%, p = 0.01).

links.outcome: AI detection sensitivity compared with radiologist assessment on the same patients
links.effect: AI was less sensitive than radiologists at patient level (76.1% vs 91.3%, p=0.02) and lesion level (71.4% vs 87.5%, p=0.01).
links.quote: The AI model performance was lower than the prospective radiology interpretation (Rad) on a patient-(AI: 76.1% vs. Rad: 91.3%, p = 0.02) and lesion-level (AI: 71.4% vs. Rad: 87.5%, p = 0.01).

links.outcome: AI sensitivity variation across treatment modality and prostate volume subgroups
links.effect: Sensitivity was higher after EBRT than brachytherapy (patient-level 81.5% vs 68.4%; lesion-level 79.4% vs 59.1%); 100% and 94.1% in glands >34 ml.
links.quote: The AI model performance was higher in EBRT group both on patient-level (EBRT: 81.5% [22/27] vs. brachytherapy: 68.4% [13/19]) and lesion-level (EBRT: 79.4% [27/34] vs. brachytherapy: 59.1% [13/22]).

screen.reason: Evaluates a pre-existing deep learning model on a new target clinical population (post-radiotherapy prostate cancer local recurrence on MRI) compared to prospective radiologist assessment, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
